stem: One humidity sensor near a dehumidifier shows a stable value while leaf symptoms cluster at the opposite end of the room. What is the strongest next step before using that sensor value to rule out an environmental contribution?
choices: Verify whether measurements are representative by comparing location, exposure, timing, and an appropriate reference or additional measurement points.
Use the single sensor because any calibrated sensor represents the whole room.
Ignore the spatial symptom pattern because sensor data always outrank crop observations.
Adjust the environmental setpoint first and verify the sensor later.
rationale: Diagnostic use of environmental data depends on representativeness and data quality; a valid reading at one location may not describe conditions elsewhere.
